rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports giving occasions of revelation for this Meccan surah often relate events merely associated with the verses; paraphrase, weak transmission, and fabrication prevent treating them as exclusive causes.
rows.anchor: فلا اعتماد في أمثال هذه السورة من السور التي نزلت دفعة

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد الله بن المهاجر
rows.claim: A report says the verse came after some people proposed that the Prophet expel the poor Companions of the Suffa.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن عبد الله بن المهاجر أن الآية نزلت في اقتراح بعض الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects that as a specific occasion because the surah was revealed all at once in Mecca, before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: ويضعفه ما تقدم في نظيره أن السورة إنما نزلت دفعة وفي مكة قبل الهجرة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Repentance before death cleanses sin and rescues from ruin; God has made mercy and forgiveness incumbent for repentant servants.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عمرو الزبيري عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال رحم الله عبدا تاب إلى الله قبل الموت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says the verse about believers coming to the Prophet was revealed concerning Ali, Hamza, and Zayd.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى وإذا جاءك الذين يؤمنون بآياتنا الآية نزلت في علي وحمزة وزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports assigning preceding verses to enemies of the Prophet’s family are applications or inner interpretations, not occasions of revelation, given the surah’s Meccan, single-period descent.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنها جميعا من قبيل الجري والتطبيق أو الأخذ بباطن المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those addressed as recipients of messengers are their communities, and the messengers are prophets; identifying the recipients as prophets and messengers as angels wrongly excludes polytheists and conflicts with context.
rows.anchor: المراد بالذين أرسل إليهم الناس وبالمرسلين الأنبياء والرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recounts people’s deeds with flawless knowledge and was never absent; this assures the truth of judgment even when recording angels were appointed.
rows.anchor: وأنه علم لا يخطئ ولا يغلط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weighing concerns deeds, or people insofar as they acted; 21:47 places it within reckoning, while 99:7–8 explicitly assigns weight to good and evil deeds.
rows.anchor: هذا الوزن من شعب حساب الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deeds erased through unbelief have no weight, so only deeds of those whose works are not nullified remain to be weighed.
rows.anchor: وبالجملة الوزن إنما هو للعمل دون عامله فالآية تثبت للعمل وزنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses portray good deeds as heavy and evil deeds as making the scales light, rather than weighing two piles and comparing their total mass.
rows.anchor: ظاهرها أن الحسنات توجب ثقل الميزان والسيئات خفة الميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic parallels consistently place heaviness with good and lightness with evil, as in 23:102–103 and 101:6–10.
rows.anchor: فالآيات كما ترى تثبت الثقل في جانب الحسنات دائما والخفة في جانب السيئات دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He proposes that each deed is tested by its own measure of truth: complete prayer, rightful almsgiving, and truthful speech exemplify standards that good deeds meet and sins fail.
rows.anchor: ففي الأعمال واحد مقياس توزن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with a physical balance illustrates a single measure placed against the item; the measure itself determines whether the item has matching weight or is rejected.
rows.anchor: والمثقال في الحقيقة هو الميزان الذي يوزن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the weight as truth contained in deeds: good works have weight to the extent they embody truth, while evil is falsehood and has none.
rows.anchor: فبقدر اشتمال العمل على الحق يكون اعتباره وقيمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The placed book identifies the truth in each deed and the weighing makes its amount manifest; he links this to judgment by truth and the book that speaks truth.
rows.anchor: فالكتاب يعين الحق وما اشتمل عليه العمل منه، والوزن يشخص مقدار الثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ‘balances’ suits the distinct standards for different acts, since the truth of prayer differs from that of almsgiving, fasting, and pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: أن لكل أحد موازين كثيرة من جهة اختلاف الحق الذي يوزن به باختلاف الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators parse ‘the weighing is the truth’ as an initial subject with ‘the truth’ describing the weighing, meaning a just weighing; he considers another parsing possible but its reading of al-Kashshaf unusual.
rows.anchor: والذي ذكره جمهور المفسرين في معنى قوله { والوزن يومئذ الحق } أن الوزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ‘balances’ means weighed deeds, as some commentators suggest, their account still leaves unclear what determines relative heaviness when good and bad acts are mixed.
rows.anchor: والأنسب بما ذكره القوم في معنى قوله { والوزن يومئذ الحق } أن يكون جمع موزون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran’s ‘just balances’ means God’s just placement, not that the balance itself is justice; the wording ‘no soul is wronged’ shows that the justice belongs to God.
rows.anchor: فالقسط قسطه وعدله فليس القسط هو الميزان يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators who take weighing as justice explain heaviness metaphorically as predominance of good deeds, and lightness as predominance of sins and loss of the self.
rows.anchor: فسروا ثقل الموازين برجحانها بنوع من التجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That interpretation must still identify a just criterion for mixed, unequal good and bad deeds; otherwise the outcome would be arbitrary and would not complete the proof against people.
rows.anchor: وإلا لزم القول بالجزاف البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He concludes that deeds are weighed by truth: those containing the truth required in worship succeed, while works lacking it leave their owners ruined for denying God’s signs.
rows.anchor: فمن ثقلت موازينه باشتمال أعماله على الحق فأولئك هم المفلحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment applies each deed to the truth proper to it; reward follows in proportion to that truth, and failure to contain it leads to ruin, so the verses can be read literally.
rows.anchor: الوزن يوم القيامة هو تطبيق الأعمال على ما هو الحق فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes weighing as justice and heavy scales as predominance of good deeds, treating the language as metaphor.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن المراد بالوزن هو العدل، وثقل الميزان هو رجحان العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects accounts that make the scales arbitrary and says each person has measures corresponding to the different truths in their deeds; the afterlife belongs wholly to truth and God.
rows.anchor: هناك بالنسبة إلى كل إنسان موازين توزن بها أعماله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Reports from Ibn Abbas say al-A‘raf was revealed in Mecca; al-Tabatabai also notes a parallel report from Ibn al-Zubayr.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال سوره الأعراف نزلت بمكة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the account of the seaside town is the one Medinan verse in al-A‘raf, with the rest Meccan.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال آية من الأعراف مدنية، وهي { واسألهم عن القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls Qatada’s classification an exegetical judgment and postpones discussion of it.
rows.anchor: أقول وهو منه اجتهاد وسيأتي ما يتعلق به من الكلام

rows.speaker: معاوية بن حيدة
rows.claim: The Prophet says God will ask whether he conveyed the message; he answers yes, orders witnesses to inform absentees, and says a person’s thigh and hand speak first when mouths are gagged.
rows.anchor: عن معاوية بن حيده أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال " إن ربي داعي وإنه سائلي هل بلغت عبادي؟

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: The Prophet says every person is a shepherd answerable for those under their care, including rulers, men, women, and servants.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال قال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم " كلكم راع وكلكم مسؤول عن رعيته

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: A report says good and evil deeds are weighed, and whichever side prevails determines entry into Paradise or Hell; the author accepts its content but not as an explanation of these verses.
rows.anchor: عن جابر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم " يوضع الميزان يوم القيامة فيوزن الحسنات والسيئات

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says a person whose outward appearance outweighs their inner state has a light scale, while inner reality outweighing outward appearance makes it heavy; the author says it does not explain the verses.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال من كان ظاهره أرجح من باطنه خفف ميزانه

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report says God fashioned the balance’s pans like heaven and earth and the path like a sword, saying he weighs and grants passage to whomever he wills.
rows.anchor: خلق الله كفتي الميزان مثل السماء والأرض فقالت الملائكة

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Al-Hakim reports a similar account from Salman.
rows.anchor: وروى الحاكم في الصحيح عن سلمان مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says these narrations depict an afterlife balance resembling the worldly instrument and are intended to make the idea accessible to unsophisticated hearers, as later reports clarify.
rows.anchor: وهي واردة لتقريب المعنى إلى الأفهام الساذجة

rows.speaker: هشام بن الحكم
rows.claim: In a debate with a skeptic, Imam al-Sadiq says deeds are attributes rather than bodies, God does not need weighing to know their amount, and the balance means justice.
rows.anchor: في حديث هشام بن الحكم عن الصادق عليه السلام أنه سأله الزنديق فقال أو ليس يوزن الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains deeds as moral qualities attached to actions, not the physical movements themselves: the same movement is lawful marriage or adultery according to its social or religious status.
rows.anchor: وإنما هي صفة ما عملوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imam’s argument has two parts: deeds as attributes have no physical weight, and God needs no weighing because nothing is hidden from him.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن الله سبحانه لا يحتاج إلى توزين الأشياء لعدم اتصافه بالجهل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some argue that embodied deeds can acquire weight, with the scale frightening sinners, encouraging the obedient, and displaying justice; they find problems in the Imam’s report.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم إنه بناء على ما هو الحق من تجسم الأعمال في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He replies that deeds may appear embodied and justice may take the form of a balance; the report denies only worldly physical weight and does not require two-pan comparison.
rows.anchor: لكن الرواية لا تنفي ذلك وإنما تنفي كون الأعمال أجساما دنيوية

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says good deeds weigh down the balance while sins make it light; the author says this supports the truth in a deed as its measure.
rows.anchor: عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام في حديث قال وأما قوله { فمن ثقلت موازينه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Asked about the just balances, Imam al-Sadiq identifies them as the prophets and their successors.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن سالم قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن قول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the report by saying prophets and Imams embody the measure of right action and belief.
rows.anchor: فإن المقياس هو حق العمل والاعتقاد، وهو الذي عندهم عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn says scales and records are set up for Muslims; polytheists are driven to Hell in groups, and he cites the verse about no weight for disbelievers.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام فيما كان يعظ به قال ثم رجع القول من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes that the narration alludes to the statement that God will not assign the disbelievers any weight on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: أقول يشير عليه السلام إلى قوله تعالى { فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qummi’s commentary interprets weighing as recompense according to deeds, good for good and evil for evil.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي في قوله { والوزن يومئذ الحق } الآية قال عليه السلام المجازاة بالأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report interprets ‘wronging Our signs’ as denying the Imams; the author treats this as one concrete instance of the broader meaning.
rows.anchor: أقول وهو من قبيل ذكر بعض المصاديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent clothing and adornment from the unseen into the visible world through creation; garments are human-made products, yet may be attributed to God as the origin of all causes and powers.
rows.anchor: فقد أنزل الله اللباس والريش بالخلق من غيب ما عنده إلى عالم الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raw cotton, wool, and silk become usable clothing through human processing; this attribution resembles ‘God created you and what you do’ and the making of natural products through many causes.
rows.anchor: فعد اللباس والريش من خلق الله وهما من عمل الإنسان نظير

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: The Manar author argues that Islam’s requirement of covering and adornment taught clothing to many peoples who had lived naked, spreading civilization and even expanding European textile trade in Africa.
rows.anchor: وأن الإسلام ما وصل إلى قوم منهم إلا وعلمهم لبس الثياب بإيجابه للستر والزينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai adds that even historically sophisticated pagan societies, especially in India, included extensive nudity; Muslim influence taught clothing and adornment to them and their neighbors.
rows.anchor: بل أقول إن بعض الأمم الوثنية ذات الحضارة والعلوم والفنون كان يغلب فيها معيشة العري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says modesty and fitting adornment increase where Islam is strong, while some Muslims in eastern lands remain closer to pagan practice in dress.
rows.anchor: فحيث يقوى الإسلام يكون الستر والزينة اللائقة بكرامة البشر ورقيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse derives a general rule from the story: communities, like individuals, have appointed lifespans, and once their term arrives they cannot delay or advance it.
rows.anchor: أن الأمم والمجتمعات لها أعمار وآجال نظير ما للأفراد من الأعمار والآجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests 7:25 concerns the life and death of each person and community within humanity’s larger lifespan, while the earlier earthly provision lasts until humanity’s extinction or resurrection.
rows.anchor: راجع إلى حياة النوع إلى حين وهو حين الانقراض أو البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic conditional ‘if messengers come’ signals certainty; recounting the signs means clarifying them, and this final universal address establishes the general religious law of following revelation through messengers.
rows.anchor: والمراد بقص الآيات بيانها وتفصيلها لما فيه من معنى القطع والإبانة

rows.speaker: موسى بن جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report identifies the indecency people falsely claimed God commanded with allegiance to unjust Imams and rulers.
rows.anchor: أن الحديث مروي عن موسى بن جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says this report does not fit the verse’s original setting, since pre-Islamic Arabs attributed customs such as naked circumambulation to God; it applies more closely to later tyrants and jurists who justified obedience to them by 4:59.
rows.anchor: فإن أهل الجاهلية كانت عندهم أحكام كثيرة متعلقة بأمور من قبيل الفحشاء

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Basir transmits the Imam’s ruling that anyone claiming God commands indecency or that good and evil belong to God has lied about him.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سمعته يقول من زعم أن الله يأمر بالفحشاء

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A second report says attributing acts to power independent of God denies his sovereignty, while denying God’s power over sins is also false and incurs punishment.
rows.anchor: عن مسعدة بن صدقة عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام من زعم أن الله أمر بالسوء والفحشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the first report’s denial of good and evil being ‘from God’ as a rejection of compulsion, and the second’s denial of God’s will as a rejection of delegation; the pronoun may also refer to delegation.
rows.anchor: ناظر إلى قول المجبرة إن الخير والشر والطاعة والمعصية إنما تستند إلى إرادة الله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: One report interprets establishing one’s face at every mosque as facing the qibla; the author calls it an application of the verse.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسكان عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سألته عن قول الله عز وجل { وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد }

rows.speaker: زرارة وحمران ومحمد بن مسلم
rows.claim: Reports from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq explain the instruction as facing the Kaaba from mosques established across the lands; the author links this to the later qibla ruling in 2:144.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة وحمران ومحمد بن مسلم عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because al-A‘raf is Meccan and the Kaaba became the qibla in Medina, this verse may state the general command, with the Medinan verse later specifying its direction.
rows.anchor: والآية التي نحن فيها وهي من سورة الاعراف مكية

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report from al-Sadiq interprets ‘establish your faces’ as the Imams; the author takes this to mean congregational prayer leaders, with another possible sense to follow.
rows.anchor: عن الحسين بن مهران عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله { وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد } يعني الأئمة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A parallel report interprets taking adornment at every mosque as the Imams; the author says presenting a worthy prayer leader beautifies worship, or it may refer to religious Imams.
rows.anchor: عن الحسين بن مهران عنه عليه السلام في قول الله { خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد } قال يعني الأئمة

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet interpreted taking adornment at every mosque as praying in one’s sandals; similar reports are related from Ali, Abu Hurayra, Ibn Mas‘ud, and others.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قول الله { خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Sent to debate Ibn al-Kawwa and his companions, Ibn Abbas defended his fine clothing by citing God’s permitted adornment and recalling the Prophet’s striped cloaks on the two Eids.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال وجهني علي بن أبي طالب إلى ابن الكواء وأصحابه

rows.speaker: فضالة بن أيوب
rows.claim: A report from al-Sadiq says to wear one’s best clothes on Eid and Friday; related versions appear in other collections and from al-Baqir.
rows.anchor: عن فضالة بن أيوب في قول الله عز وجل { خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد } قال في العيد والجمعة

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Asked about the verse, al-Rida says that combing before every prayer is among its applications.
rows.anchor: سئل أبو الحسن الرضا عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل { خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد } قال من ذلك التمشط عند كل صلاة

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Hasan wore his finest clothes for prayer because God loves beauty and asks worshippers to take their adornment at every mosque.
rows.anchor: عن خيثمة بن أبي خيثمة قال كان الحسن بن علي عليه السلام إذا قام إلى الصلاة لبس أجود ثيابه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq permits fine khazz garments and invokes the example of al-Husayn’s clothing; he also retells Ibn Abbas’s argument from the verses permitting adornment and good provisions.
rows.anchor: عن يونس بن إبراهيم قال دخلت يوما على أبي عبد الله عليه السلام وعلي جبة خز

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: When Sufyan al-Thawri objects to his costly clothes, al-Sadiq says the Prophet lived in straitened times but the world later opened, and the righteous are most entitled to its lawful goods.
rows.anchor: مر سفيان الثوري في المسجد الحرام فرأى أبا عبد الله عليه السلام وعليه أثواب كثيرة قيمة حسان

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq tells Sufyan that his visible fine robe is for people while a coarse garment underneath is for himself; Sufyan’s rough outer and soft inner clothes reveal the reverse.
rows.anchor: هذا لبسته لنفسي وما رأيته للناس ثم جذب ثوبا على سفيان أعلاه غليظا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq rebukes Abbad ibn Kathir for forbidding fine dress and says God loves to see the effects of his blessing on a servant.
rows.anchor: عن ابن القداح قال كان أبو عبد الله عليه السلام متكئا علي فلقيه عباد بن كثير

rows.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that God loves to see the effects of his blessing on his servant.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله يحب أن يرى أثر نعمته

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Rida says Ali ibn al-Husayn wore expensive silk-lined robes in winter, then sold them after winter and gave the proceeds to charity, citing the permission of adornment and good provisions.
rows.anchor: فإن علي بن الحسين كان يلبس الجبة الخز بخمس مائة درهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes that reports on these permissions and practices are numerous.
rows.anchor: أقول والروايات في هذه المعاني كثيرة جدا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says wealth belongs to God and is entrusted to people, who may use it moderately for food, drink, clothing, marriage, and transport while directing the surplus to poor believers; excess is forbidden.
rows.anchor: أترى الله ائتمن رجلا على مال خول له أن يشتري فرسا بعشرة آلاف درهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: He illustrates waste by asking whether an entrusted person should buy an extravagant horse or concubine at many times its value, then quotes the ban on excess.
rows.anchor: ويشتري جارية بألف دينار ويجزيه جارية بعشرين دينارا وقال ولا تسرفوا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Asked about flour used after depilatory treatment when no bran is available, al-Sadiq says what repairs the body is not waste; waste damages wealth or health, and moderation includes varied ordinary foods.
rows.anchor: عن إسحاق بن عبد العزيز عن بعض أصحابه عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال نكون بطريق مكة

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Kazim explains visible indecency as public adultery and prostitution flags, hidden indecency as marrying a deceased father’s non-mother wife, and ‘sin’ as wine.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن يقطين عن أبي الحسن عليه السلام قال قال قول الله عز وجل { قل إنما حرم ربي الفواحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the report condenses al-Kazim’s debate with al-Mahdi and points to fuller versions elsewhere.
rows.anchor: والرواية ملخصة من كلامه عليه السلام مع المهدي

rows.speaker: موسى بن جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says Quranic prohibitions have an outward legal sense and a hidden sense referring to unjust Imams, while permitted things also point inwardly to the Imams of truth.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن منصور قال سألت عبدا صالحا عليه السلام عن قول الله { إنما حرم ربي الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the inward mapping by saying each group draws people toward God or away from him and toward its characteristic actions.
rows.anchor: لكون كل واحد من الطائفتين سببا للقرب من الله أو البعد عنه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq interprets taking adornment at every mosque as washing when meeting each Imam; the author groups this with earlier reports about Imams.
rows.anchor: عن العلاء بن سيابة عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد } قال الغسل

rows.speaker: سعد بن عبادة
rows.claim: After Sa‘d ibn Ubada says he would strike a man found with his wife, the Prophet says God is more jealous than Sa‘d or himself and forbids outward and inward indecencies.
rows.anchor: عن المغيرة ابن شعبة قال قال سعد بن عبادة لو رأيت رجلا مع امرأتي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq transmits the Prophet’s statement that none is more jealous than God, who forbids public and hidden indecencies.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي حمزة قال سمعت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام يقول قال النبي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Asked about the appointed term, al-Sadiq says it is what has been assigned to the Angel of Death; the author links this to earlier reports on 6:2.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله { إذا جاء أجلهم فلا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون } قال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says people were created as believers or unbelievers, happy or wretched, and return on Judgment Day as guided or astray; Ali ibn Ibrahim also quotes the Prophet that happiness or misery is fixed in the womb.
rows.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { كما بدأكم تعودون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though Abu al-Jarud is criticized, transmitters accepted his reports from al-Baqir before his deviation; other reports also convey the return’s resemblance to the beginning.
rows.anchor: القوم قبلوا ما رواه عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في حال استقامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects essential, inescapable happiness or misery: it would make education, moral judgment, law, revelation, and completing the proof against people meaningless, and would limit God’s sovereignty.
rows.anchor: ولا معنى لإتمام الحجة في الذاتيات بأي معنى صورناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran affirms human choice: God creates people, grants reason to distinguish good from evil, then tests them through religious duties; obedience yields reward and disobedience punishment.
rows.anchor: والدار دار امتحان وابتلاء، والعمل اليوم والجزاء غدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This account rests on two premises: voluntary action differs from involuntary action, and chosen acts can be morally good or bad and merit praise, blame, reward, or punishment.
rows.anchor: إحداهما أن بين الفعل الاختياري وغيره فرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: General reports that humanity was created as two groups match verses describing believers and unbelievers; the division is initially general and each person’s outcome becomes definite through chosen deeds and guidance or satanic influence.
rows.anchor: الذي في بدء الخلقة قضاء مشروط ثم يخرج عن الاشتراط إلى الإطلاق بالأعمال الاختيارية

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sajjad says God made the Shia from a high heavenly clay, their enemies from Sijjin, and the enemies’ allies from an even lower clay.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام أنه قال أخذ الله ميثاق شيعتنا معنا على ولايتنا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Asked why some non-Shia show fine manners while some Shia behave badly, al-Sadiq says human clay was mixed from Paradise and Fire and people return toward the material that marked them.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن كيسان قال قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام جعلت فداك أنا مولاك

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali is reported to say Adam was created from varied earth—salty, barren, and wholesome—and his descendants include the righteous and wicked.
rows.anchor: عن حبة العرني عن علي عليه السلام قال إن الله خلق آدم من أديم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects the clay reports to the Quranic books of the wicked in Sijjin and the righteous in Illiyun.
rows.anchor: إن كتاب الفجار لفي سجين وما أدراك ما سجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report about Adam’s diverse earth suggests material constitution influences human traits, as different materials shape the forms and effects that arise from them, but only as a predisposition, not a complete cause.
rows.anchor: وإن كان ذلك على الاقتضاء دون العلية التامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He interprets Paradise or Fire clay as earthly matter that ultimately becomes part of the corresponding afterlife realm through a person’s development and deeds.
rows.anchor: إنما يسلك إلى كل منهما ما يناسبها في مادة الخلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Healthy temperaments can produce finer spirits, understanding, and emotions that incline people toward sound belief, intention, and action; the same process applies to misery.
rows.anchor: تنشأ ذوات أرواح لطيفة لها عقول جيدة وعواطف رقيقة تميل بالإنسان إلى ما فيه صلاح إنسانيته من العقائد والإرادات والأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good temperaments and spirits incline people toward sound belief, intention, and action; the influences accumulate toward an outcome, with the same reasoning applying to misery.
rows.anchor: لها عقول جيدة وعواطف رقيقة تميل بالإنسان إلى ما فيه صلاح إنسانيته
